items.rationale: Explains the SQL syntax and parameters for deduplication in Flink.
items.title: Flink Deduplication Syntax
items.statement: Flink deduplication uses ROW_NUMBER() with PARTITION BY and ORDER BY time attributes to remove duplicates.
items.quote: SELECT [column_list] FROM table_name QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER ([PARTITION BY col1[, col2...]] ORDER BY time_attr [asc|desc]) = 1

items.rationale: The optimizer requires exact adherence to the deduplication pattern to work correctly.
items.title: Follow Exact Deduplication Pattern
items.statement: The deduplication query must follow the exact pattern for Flink's optimizer to recognize it.
items.quote: the above pattern must be followed exactly, otherwise the optimizer won’t be able to translate the query.

items.rationale: Explains how Flink implements deduplication.
items.title: Flink Deduplication Mechanism
items.statement: Flink treats deduplication as a special case of Top-N where N is one and ordered by processing or event time.
items.quote: deduplication is a special case of Top-N in which the N is one and order by the processing time or event time.

items.rationale: Provides a concrete example of deduplication in Flink SQL.
items.title: Example Deduplication Query
items.statement: An example query shows how to remove duplicate rows on order_id while keeping the first occurrence.
items.quote: SELECT order_id, user, product, num FROM ( SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY proctime ASC) AS row_num FROM Orders) WHERE row_num = 1

items.title: OVER Aggregates vs GROUP BY
items.statement: OVER aggregates compute an aggregated value for every input row over a range of ordered rows, unlike GROUP BY which reduces rows to one per group.
items.quote: `OVER` aggregates compute an aggregated value for every input row over a range of ordered rows. In contrast to `GROUP BY` aggregates, `OVER` aggregates do not reduce the number of result rows to a single row for every group.

items.title: Mandatory ORDER BY in OVER Windows
items.statement: OVER windows must include an ORDER BY clause because tables lack inherent order.
items.quote: `OVER` windows are defined on an ordered sequence of rows. Since tables do not have an inherent order, the `ORDER BY` clause is mandatory.

items.rationale: Flink's current limitation requires identical OVER windows for all aggregates in streaming queries.
items.title: Identical OVER Windows for Streaming
items.statement: In streaming queries, all OVER windows for aggregates must be identical due to a current limitation.
items.quote: for streaming queries, the `OVER` windows for all aggregates must be identical due to current limitation.

items.title: RANGE vs ROWS Intervals

items.quote: Both Table API and DataStream API are equally important when it comes to defining a data processing pipeline.

items.rationale: Avoid adding new syntax for a rare case; resume() already handles recovery by starting a new job without deleting data, and logging a warning suffices.
items.title: No flag for resume() on ACTIVATED tables
items.statement: The project decided not to add a flag (e.g., FORCE) for resume() on ACTIVATED tables, as resume() already recovers by starting a new job without deleting data.
items.quote: I'd rather not like to add one at this point. RESUME on an ACTIVATED table is already a recovery-only call.

items.rationale: Ensures consistency with SQL behavior and avoids complexity in conflict detection.
items.title: Apply MaterializedTableEvolution changes in call order
items.statement: Changes in MaterializedTableEvolution must be applied in the order they are invoked, with each change modifying the result of the previous one.
items.quote: I would propose to apply changes in call order, each to the result of the earlier ones

items.rationale: Prevents unsupported queries from being materialized and ensures users are aware of limitations.
items.title: Reject unsupported queries in materializeInto()
items.statement: Queries without SQL serialization (e.g., session windows) must be rejected with a ValidationException before catalog writes.
items.quote: queries that have no SQL serialization yet, like session windows, would be rejected at materializeInto(...) with a ValidationException

items.rationale: Clarifies behavior for Table API vs. SQL-defined materialized tables.
items.title: getOriginalQuery() and getExpandedQuery() behavior
items.statement: For Table API-defined materialized tables, both methods return the same generated SQL, while for SQL-defined tables, getOriginalQuery() returns user-written SQL and getExpandedQuery() returns the validated, fully qualified query.
items.quote: For a materialized table declared from the Table API both would return the same SQL, generated by QueryOperation#asSerializableString().

items.rationale: Guides users on when it is safe to use resume() for recovery.
items.title: Resume() for ACTIVATED tables
items.statement: Resume() can recover an ACTIVATED table whose refresh job has disappeared, but should only be used once the old job can no longer write.
items.quote: resume() should log a warning that names the cluster it checked, and the docs should state that a table should only be resumed once its old refresh job can no longer write.

items.rationale: The resume position is built from a static starting offset, causing replay of all data since task start on cursor recreation.
items.title: Cursor recreation uses static starting offset
items.statement: Recreating the MongoDB CDC change stream cursor uses the task's starting offset, which never advances, leading to replay of all events since task start.
items.quote: the fetch task recreates the cursor in place [1], but builds the resume position from streamSplit.getStartingOffset() [2] -- which is set when the task starts and never advances.

items.rationale: The error log lacks specificity, making it hard to diagnose which error triggered cursor recreation.
items.title: Error log lacks error code
items.statement: The log message for cursor recreation does not include the error code or message, making it impossible to identify which of the six possible errors occurred.
items.quote: the only log line is a fixed WARN, "Change stream cursor has expired, trying to recreate cursor" [4], with no error code or message.

items.rationale: BSONObjectTooLarge errors cannot be resolved by cursor recreation because the event itself is too large.
items.title: BSONObjectTooLarge cannot be fixed by recreation
items.statement: Recreating the cursor does not resolve BSONObjectTooLarge errors because the event itself exceeds the 16MB limit.
items.quote: It's in the recreate list [5], but recreating can't help since the event itself is too large.

items.rationale: Proposed fix to track the latest resume token for accurate cursor recreation.
items.title: Track latest resume token
items.statement: The system must track the latest resume token (including events and heartbeats) to reopen the cursor from the correct position.
items.quote: Track the latest resume token (events + heartbeats) and reopen from it.

items.quote: 如果你看到一个 task 发生 **反压警告**（例如： `High`），意味着它生产数据的速率比下游 task 消费数据的速率要快。

items.title: Backpressure propagation
items.statement: Backpressure propagates upstream against the data flow direction.
items.quote: 反压沿着相反的方向传播，沿着数据流向上游传播。

items.title: Backpressure detection
items.statement: Backpressure is determined by the availability of output buffers in a task.
items.quote: 在内部，反压根据输出 buffers 的可用性来进行判断的。

items.title: Backpressure state thresholds
items.statement: Backpressure states are categorized as OK (0-10%), LOW (10-50%), or HIGH (50-100%).

items.statement: The default managed-memory path closes the state handler before stopping Beam requests, which can cause IllegalStateException during shutdown callbacks.

Consequently, close() gates stateRequestHandler before releasing sharedResources; the actual shared factory closes afterward—or remains active until the final lease. Shutdown callbacks can therefore receive IllegalStateException

items.title: ML_PREDICT Function Purpose
items.statement: Flink SQL provides the ML_PREDICT table-valued function to perform model inference directly in SQL queries.
items.quote: Flink SQL 提供了 `ML_PREDICT` 表值函数（TVF）来在 SQL 查询中执行模型推理。

items.title: Model Registration Requirement
items.statement: A model must be registered in the catalog before using ML_PREDICT.
items.quote: 在使用 `ML_PREDICT` 之前，模型必须在目录中注册。

items.title: Feature Column Matching
items.statement: The number of feature columns specified in the descriptor must match the model's input schema.
items.quote: 描述符中指定的特征列数量必须与模型的输入模式匹配。

items.title: Avoid CDC Tables
items.statement: ML_PREDICT only supports append-only tables and does not support CDC tables due to non-deterministic results.
items.quote: `ML_PREDICT` 仅支持仅追加表。不支持 CDC（变更数据捕获）表，因为 `ML_PREDICT` 的结果是非确定性的。

items.title: Async Inference for High Throughput
items.statement: For high-throughput scenarios, consider using asynchronous inference mode.
items.quote: 对于高吞吐量场景，考虑使用异步推理模式。

items.title: OVER Aggregation Basics
items.statement: OVER aggregation computes aggregate values for each row in a sorted range without reducing the result to a single row per group.
items.quote: `OVER` 聚合通过排序后的范围数据为每行输入计算出聚合值。和 `GROUP BY` 聚合不同， `OVER` 聚合不会把结果通过分组减少到一行，它会为每行输入增加一个聚合值。

items.rationale: Flink's streaming queries currently require all OVER window definitions to be identical.
items.title: Streaming Query OVER Window Constraint
items.statement: In streaming queries, all OVER window definitions must be identical.
items.quote: 对于流式查询，由于目前的限制，所有聚合的 `OVER` 窗口必须是相同的。

items.title: OVER Window Syntax
items.statement: OVER window syntax includes PARTITION BY, ORDER BY, and range/row definitions.
items.quote: SELECT agg_func(agg_col) OVER ( [PARTITION BY col1[, col2, ...]] ORDER BY time_col|non_time_col range_definition|row_definition), ... FROM ...

items.title: Flink RANGE Interval Support
items.statement: Flink supports RANGE intervals defined on time attributes with CURRENT ROW as the upper bound.
items.quote: Flink 只支持 `CURRENT ROW` 作为上边界。

items.title: Purpose of SQL Hints
items.statement: SQL hints are used to modify execution plans, enhance the planner, add dynamic metadata, or constrain operator resources.
items.quote: SQL 提示（SQL Hints）是和 SQL 语句一起使用来改变执行计划的。

items.title: Dynamic Table Options Syntax
items.statement: Dynamic table options can be specified using Oracle-style SQL hints syntax to override table options per query.
items.quote: table_path /*+ OPTIONS(key=val [, key=val]*) */

items.rationale: Flink enforces a single hint block per query block to avoid parsing errors.
items.title: Single Hint Block per Query
items.statement: Only one hint block is allowed per query block in Flink to prevent SQL parsing errors.
items.quote: Flink 联接提示在一个查询块（Query Block）中只支持定义一个提示块

items.title: BROADCAST Join Limitations
items.statement: BROADCAST join hints only work with equi-join conditions and do not support Full Outer Join.
items.quote: BROADCAST 只支持等值的联接条件，且不支持 Full Outer Join。

items.title: LOOKUP Hint Options
items.statement: The LOOKUP hint allows configuring synchronous/asynchronous lookup functions, retry strategies, and parameters like timeout and capacity.
items.quote: LOOKUP 联接提示允许用户建议 Flink 优化器: 1. 使用同步或异步的查找函数 2. 配置异步查找相关参数 3. 启用延迟重试查找策略

items.title: Definition of Determinism
items.statement: An operation is deterministic if it always produces identical results with identical input values.

items.title: Dynamic vs Non-Deterministic Functions

items.quote: The non-deterministic functions are executed at runtime (in clusters, evaluated per record), while the dynamic functions determine the corresponding values only when the query plan is generated

items.title: Flink's Determinism Scope

items.quote: the determinism provided is limited to the computation only, because it does not store user data itself

items.title: Dynamic tables are logical

items.quote: Dynamic tables are foremost a logical concept. Dynamic tables are not necessarily (fully) materialized during query execution.

items.title: Continuous queries semantics

items.quote: a continuous query output is always semantically equivalent to the result of the same query executed in batch mode on a snapshot of the input tables.

items.title: Dynamic tables change over time

items.title: Streaming query never completes

items.rationale: Explains the root cause of the non-deterministic results in mini-batch two-phase aggregation.
items.title: Mini-batch aggregation issue cause
items.statement: MiniBatchLocalGroupAggFunction resets the accumulator per bundle, causing incorrect counts and lost values during retraction and accumulation.
items.quote: MiniBatchLocalGroupAggFunction starts each bundle from a fresh accumulator, so a bundle that begins with -U takes the local count to -1. WelfordM2AggFunction.accumulate / retract return early while acc.n <= 0 (dropping the value), and merge only adds the count of a partial accumulator with n <= 0, so the retracted and the new value are both lost.

items.rationale: The TTL mechanism in PyFlink fails to disable the read cache in Apache Beam 2.43.0+ due to a change in how Beam's StateCache checks cache enablement.

items.rationale: Explicitly configuring both total process memory and total Flink memory may lead to deployment failures due to potential memory configuration conflicts.

items.statement: Do not configure both total process memory and total Flink memory simultaneously to prevent conflicts.

items.title: Network buffer queues impact throughput and checkpoints
items.statement: Larger in-flight data improves throughput but increases checkpoint times due to barrier propagation or size.
items.quote: Having a larger amount of in-flight data means that Flink can provide higher and more resilient throughput in the pipeline. This will, however, cause longer checkpoint times.

items.rationale: Avoids silent performance degradation or task failures due to buffer shortages.
items.title: Do not change read-buffer threshold
items.statement: Users should not modify the `taskmanager.network.memory.read-buffer.required-per-gate.max` threshold unless they have strong reasons.
items.quote: We do not recommend users to change this threshold, unless the user has good reasons and knows what he/she is doing well.

items.title: Buffer debloating limitations with multiple inputs
items.statement: Buffer debloating may misallocate buffers for subtasks with multiple inputs of vastly different throughputs.
items.quote: If your subtask has multiple different inputs or it has a single but unioned input, buffer debloating can cause the input of the low throughput to have too much buffered in-flight data, while the input of the high throughput might have buffers that are too small to sustain that throughput.

items.title: High parallelism may break buffer debloating
items.statement: Buffer debloating may fail with high parallelism (above ~200) using default settings, requiring increased floating buffers.
items.quote: Currently, the buffer debloating mechanism might not perform correctly with high parallelism (above ~200) using the default configuration.

items.rationale: Identifies the root cause of the SinkV2ITCase test failure as an exactly-once data-loss bug.
items.title: Root cause of SinkV2ITCase failure
items.statement: SinkV2 jobs with a post-commit global committer can lose the final checkpoint's committables under unaligned checkpoints due to premature EndOfData broadcast.
items.quote: SinkV2 jobs with a post-commit (global) committer can lose the final checkpoint's committables under unaligned checkpoints

items.rationale: The proposed fix ensures committables are delivered before downstream tasks finish.
items.title: Fix for SinkV2ITCase data loss
items.statement: Defer downstream EndOfData broadcast until the final checkpoint completes for tasks emitting records on the final checkpoint.
items.quote: Defer the downstream EndOfData broadcast - for tasks whose operator chain emits records on the final checkpoint - until the final checkpoint completes

items.rationale: Explains why the bug surfaces intermittently in CI.

items.statement: The bug only surfaces under CI checkpoint randomization because aligned checkpoints mask the issue by delivering committables normally.
items.quote: With aligned checkpoints the last committables fall into a pre-end-of-input checkpoint and are delivered normally, which is why it only surfaces intermittently under the CI checkpoint randomization.

items.rationale: Highlights that the issue is not flaky but a real data-loss bug.

items.title: Window TVF bug in inferRowType
items.statement: The inferRowType() method in SqlWindowTableFunction.java incorrectly preserves the ROWTIME attribute on the original time column instead of materializing it to a regular TIMESTAMP.
items.quote: This method constructs the output schema of all window TVFs (TUMBLE/HOP/CUMULATE) via ARG0_TABLE_FUNCTION_WINDOWING. It uses .addAll(inputRowType.getFieldList()) to copy all input fields into the output, which blindly preserves the TimeIndicatorRelDataType (ROWTIME) on the original time column instead of materializing it to a regular TIMESTAMP.

items.title: MiniBatch Aggregation Reduces State Overhead
items.statement: Mini-batch aggregation caches input records in a buffer to reduce state access overhead, trading latency for throughput.
items.quote: The core idea of mini-batch aggregation is caching a bundle of inputs in a buffer inside of the aggregation operator. When the bundle of inputs is triggered to process, only one operation per key to access state is needed. This can significantly reduce the state overhead and get a better throughput. However, this may increase some latency because it buffers some records instead of processing them in an instant.

items.title: Enable MiniBatch Aggregation
items.statement: To enable mini-batch aggregation, set `table.exec.mini-batch.enabled`, `table.exec.mini-batch.allow-latency`, and `table.exec.mini-batch.size` in the Flink configuration.
items.quote: In order to enable this optimization, you should set options `table.exec.mini-batch.enabled`, `table.exec.mini-batch.allow-latency` and `table.exec.mini-batch.size`.

items.title: Local-Global Aggregation Solves Data Skew
items.statement: Local-global aggregation splits group aggregation into local and global stages to mitigate data skew and reduce network shuffle.
items.quote: Local-Global is proposed to solve data skew problem by dividing a group aggregation into two stages, that is doing local aggregation in upstream firstly, and followed by global aggregation in downstream.

items.title: Enable Local-Global Aggregation
items.statement: To enable local-global aggregation, set `table.optimizer.agg-phase-strategy` to `TWO_PHASE` and ensure mini-batch is enabled.
items.quote: configuration.set("table.optimizer.agg-phase-strategy", "TWO_PHASE"); // enable two-phase, i.e. local-global aggregation

items.title: Temporal Table Function Purpose
items.statement: A temporal table function provides access to the version of a temporal table at a specific point in time.
items.quote: A Temporal table function provides access to the version of a temporal table at a specific point in time.

items.rationale: Temporal table functions are restricted to append-only streams to ensure consistency in versioning.
items.title: Append-Only Stream Requirement
items.statement: Temporal table functions can only be defined on top of append-only streams.
items.quote: Unlike a versioned table, temporal table functions can only be defined on top of append-only streams

items.rationale: Pure SQL DDL does not support the definition of temporal table functions, requiring the use of the Table API.

items.statement: A temporal table function cannot be defined in pure SQL DDL.
items.quote: Additionally, a temporal table function cannot be defined in pure SQL DDL.

items.title: Join with Temporal Table Function
items.statement: Append-only tables can join with a temporal table to retrieve historical values for a key at a specific time.
items.quote: Append-only tables (left input/probe side) can join with a temporal table (right input/build side), i.e., a table that changes over time and tracks its changes, to retrieve the value for a key as it was at a particular point in time.

items.title: Continuous Query Semantics
items.statement: A continuous query on a dynamic table never terminates and updates its result table to reflect changes in the input table.
items.quote: 查询不断更新其(动态)结果表，以反映其(动态)输入表上的更改。

items.title: Stream to Table Conversion
items.statement: A stream can be converted to a table by interpreting each record as an INSERT operation, forming an INSERT-only changelog stream.
items.quote: 从概念上讲，流的每条记录都被解释为对结果表的 `INSERT` 操作。本质上我们正在从一个 `INSERT`-only 的 changelog 流构建表。

items.title: Continuous Query Limitations
items.statement: Some continuous queries may be too expensive to compute due to large state size or high cost of updating results.
items.quote: 有些查询代价太高而无法计算，这可能是由于它们需要维护的状态大小，也可能是由于计算更新代价太高。

items.rationale: Explains the type inference mechanism for procedures in Flink.
items.title: Flink Procedure Type Inference
items.statement: Flink automatically infers data types for procedure parameters and return types via reflection, but can be supported with `@DataTypeHint` and `@ProcedureHint` annotations.
items.quote: Flink's procedures implement an automatic type inference extraction that derives data types from the procedure's class and its `call` methods via reflection. If this implicit reflective extraction approach is not successful, the extraction process can be supported by annotating affected parameters, classes, or methods with `@DataTypeHint` and `@ProcedureHint`.

items.title: Parallelism in Flink
items.statement: A Flink program consists of tasks, each with multiple parallel instances, and the number of instances is called the task's parallelism.
items.quote: 一个 Flink 程序由多个任务 task 组成（转换/算子、数据源和数据接收器）。一个 task 包括多个并行执行的实例，且每一个实例都处理 task 输入数据的一个子集。一个 task 的并行实例数被称为该 task 的 *并行度* (parallelism)。

items.rationale: Setting a very large max parallelism degrades performance due to state backend overhead and key-group expansion.
items.title: Avoid excessive max parallelism
items.statement: Avoid setting an extremely high maximum parallelism as it can degrade performance.
items.quote: 为最大并行度设置一个非常大的值将会降低性能，因为一些 state backends 需要维持内部的数据结构，而这些数据结构将会随着 key-groups 的数目而扩张

items.title: Set parallelism at operator level
items.statement: You can set the parallelism for individual operators, data sources, or sinks using the `setParallelism()` method.
items.quote: 单个算子、数据源和数据接收器的并行度可以通过调用 `setParallelism()`方法来指定。

items.title: Set default parallelism at environment level
items.statement: The default parallelism for all operators, sources, and sinks can be set at the execution environment level using `setParallelism()`.
items.quote: 可以通过调用 `setParallelism()` 方法指定执行环境的默认并行度。

items.title: State incompatibility with max parallelism change
items.statement: Changing the maximum parallelism when restoring from a previous job can cause state incompatibility.
items.quote: 从之前的作业恢复时，改变该作业的最大并发度将会导致状态不兼容。

items.rationale: Weighting allocation based on subtask throughput or active split count addresses unequal split assignment and partition skew, improving total throughput.

items.statement: Ramin represented Flink at Community Over Code 2026 with Sergey Nuyanzin on Materialized Tables.
items.quote: Ramin represented Flink at Community Over Code 2026 together with Sergey Nuyanzin, about “Enterprise-Grade Data Pipelines: The Evolution of Flink Materialized Tables”

items.title: Ramin's New Committer Status
items.statement: Ramin Gharib accepted the invitation to become a Flink Committer.
items.quote: Ramin Gharib has accepted the invitation to become a Flink Committer

items.rationale: To avoid breaking rollback safety for earlier Flink versions, the feature should be opt-in initially.
items.title: Default coordinator-state-in-file.enabled to false
items.statement: The option execution.checkpointing.coordinator-state-in-file.enabled defaults to false to preserve rollback safety.
items.quote: I’ve updated the FLIP to default execution.checkpointing.coordinator-state-in-file.enabled to false.

items.rationale: To allow independent tuning of coordinator state and task state thresholds.
items.title: Separate threshold for coordinator state
items.statement: A new option execution.checkpointing.coordinator-state-inline-threshold must be introduced to control coordinator state independently of task state.
items.quote: I’ve added execution.checkpointing.coordinator-state-inline-threshold to the FLIP and the prototype

items.rationale: The current default threshold for inline data is 20 KB, which is too restrictive for coordinator state.
items.title: Default data-inline-threshold is 20 KB
items.statement: The existing execution.checkpointing.data-inline-threshold defaults to 20 KB and also controls task state.
items.quote: The existing execution.checkpointing.data-inline-threshold defaults to 20 KB and also controls task state.

items.rationale: Reusing the same threshold for coordinator state and task state can lead to unintended side effects.
items.title: Avoid reusing data-inline-threshold for coordinator state
items.statement: Reusing execution.checkpointing.data-inline-threshold for coordinator state may create many small files or alter task-state behavior.
items.quote: Reusing it means that enabling this feature may create many small coordinator state files, while increasing it would also change task-state behavior.

items.rationale: Preview releases are not intended for production use, so functional testing is deprioritized.
items.title: Preview releases skip production testing
items.statement: Preview releases like Flink Agents 0.4.0 must not be used in production, and functional tests should not be the focus of verification.
items.quote: Flink Agents 0.4.0 is a preview release and should not be used in production environments. Therefore, functionality tests should not be the focus of verifications for this release candidate.

items.rationale: The signing key fingerprint is a critical detail for verifying release artifacts.
items.title: Release signing key fingerprint
items.statement: The official Apache Flink Agents release artifacts are signed with the key fingerprint 08F0B88DCB04DD4E.
items.quote: signed with the key with fingerprint 08F0B88DCB04DD4E

items.rationale: Operator snapshots with pending actions may not restore correctly during upgrades, which is a known limitation.
items.title: Snapshot restoration limitation
items.statement: Operator snapshots taken while an action is pending may not restore correctly during upgrades, even across multiple versions.
items.quote: operator snapshots taken while an action was still pending didn't restore on the next release

items.rationale: Building the Python wheel requires pointing to the staging repository until artifacts are on Maven Central.
items.title: Python wheel installation from staging
items.statement: To install the Python wheel from the staging repository, set FLINK_AGENTS_MAVEN_MIRROR to the staging repo URL.
items.quote: installs with FLINK_AGENTS_MAVEN_MIRROR pointed at the staging repo (plain pip install 404s until the jars are on Maven Central)

items.rationale: The vote requires a minimum number of affirmative votes from PMC members to pass.
items.title: Vote adoption criteria
items.statement: The release vote must be adopted by majority approval with at least 3 PMC affirmative votes.
items.quote: It is adopted by majority approval, with at least 3 PMC affirmative votes.

items.rationale: Avoid adding new syntax for a rare case; resume() already handles recovery by starting a new job without deleting data, and logging a warning suffices.
items.title: No flag for resume() on ACTIVATED tables
items.statement: The project decided not to add a flag (e.g., FORCE) for resume() on ACTIVATED tables, as resume() already recovers by starting a new job without deleting data.
items.quote: I'd rather not like to add one at this point. RESUME on an ACTIVATED table is already a recovery-only call.

items.rationale: Ensures consistency with SQL behavior and avoids complexity in conflict detection.
items.title: Apply MaterializedTableEvolution changes in call order
items.statement: Changes in MaterializedTableEvolution must be applied in the order they are invoked, with each change modifying the result of the previous one.
items.quote: I would propose to apply changes in call order, each to the result of the earlier ones

items.rationale: Prevents unsupported queries from being materialized and ensures users are aware of limitations.
items.title: Reject unsupported queries in materializeInto()
items.statement: Queries without SQL serialization (e.g., session windows) must be rejected with a ValidationException before catalog writes.
items.quote: queries that have no SQL serialization yet, like session windows, would be rejected at materializeInto(...) with a ValidationException

items.rationale: Clarifies behavior for Table API vs. SQL-defined materialized tables.
items.title: getOriginalQuery() and getExpandedQuery() behavior
items.statement: For Table API-defined materialized tables, both methods return the same generated SQL, while for SQL-defined tables, getOriginalQuery() returns user-written SQL and getExpandedQuery() returns the validated, fully qualified query.
items.quote: For a materialized table declared from the Table API both would return the same SQL, generated by QueryOperation#asSerializableString().

items.rationale: Guides users on when it is safe to use resume() for recovery.
items.title: Resume() for ACTIVATED tables
items.statement: Resume() can recover an ACTIVATED table whose refresh job has disappeared, but should only be used once the old job can no longer write.
items.quote: resume() should log a warning that names the cluster it checked, and the docs should state that a table should only be resumed once its old refresh job can no longer write.
